In an ultimate bit of disrespect, the Detroit Pistons are resting star Cade Cunningham tonight against the New Orleans Pelicans. The reasoning appears to be twofold — 1. Cunningham played last night. 2. The Pelicans. The poor, beleaguered Pelicans, home to former Pistons executives Joe Dumars and Troy Weaver, are not having a smooth go of it early in the season. They are 5-10, the coach is fighting with players, and a starter has already asked for a trade. That doesn’t mean there isn’t talent on the team. In fact, Dumars is being ridiculed because he’s asking for the moon and the stars from other GMs interested in some of his very useful players. That means the Pistons could very well drop a game tonight coming off the high of an absolutely gutsy performance against the San Antonio Spurs. But it also means that Detroit thinks it also has a pretty decent shot to win even without their superstar player. The good news is that while Cunningham, Jalen Duren, Duncan Robinson and Ron Holland all remain out, we might see Isaiah Joe back in a Pistons uniform.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Pelicans preview:  Closing out the road trip in New Orleans
pistons.body:
The Pistons have played a lot of road games so far this season.  They have also played less games than a lot of other teams because of that.  Last night’s game against the San Antonio Spurs was probably their toughest test of the season so far, and they passed it with flying colors.

The Spurs were in the midst of a 12 game winning streak and playing at home against a Pistons team down 4 players who were in their opening night rotation.  Despite that, they went into San Antonio and imposed their will and came out on top.

Now, they head to New Orleans to close out this 4-game road trip against a Pelicans team that has struggled this season.  After a game like last night, these are the exact kind of games that can be a bit of a trap, so hopefully the Pistons come out ready to play and close out this road trip with a 3-1 record.

The Pistons are still set to be short-handed, but as they proved last night, that doesn’t matter to this team.

Game Vitals

Where:  Smoothie King Center in New Orleans, LA
When:  Wednesday, November 18 at 8 pm EST
Watch:  Scripps Sports Network
Odds:  Pistons (-7.5)

Analysis

I mentioned the Pistons injuries above, as they are expected to once again be without Isaiah Joe, Duncan Robinson, Taurean Prince, Ron Holland, and Jalen Duren.  However, New Orleans is also without a slew of rotation players like Benedict Mathurin, Trey Murphy III, and Dejounte Murray.  The biggest difference is the Pistons have one of the deepest rosters in the league to overcome missing some key players while the Pelicans have a less talented roster.

None of that is to say that this game will be easy, but after a hard-fought battle against the Spurs last night, it will be nice to not have to deal with an imposing force like Victor Wembanyama again.

The Pistons depth was put to the test against the Spurs and the Pistons proved why they are one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference by coming out on top.  Of course, it was led by great 2-way performances by Cade Cunningham and Ausar Thompson, but that is to be expected of the Pistons two stars.

The Pelicans don’t present that same size-related issues the Pistons have had to deal with in their last few games, which is lucky for them.  The Pelicans do have a couple of players capable of taking over a game, like Jordan Poole and Zion Williamson, so it is important that the Pistons stay disciplined on defense, but Zion Williamson at least doesn’t tower over players like Ausar Thompson, who has had to take on more big matchups with the Pistons opting to start John Collins at center.

The Collins at center lineup has had a bit of diminishing returns lately as he has struggled to deal with size and rebounding, but it has allowed the Pistons to start Daniss Jenkins, who has been on a heater lately.  He had 25 points, 5 rebounds, and 5 assists last night against the Spurs and a couple of clutch shots.  He also had 21 and 22 points in back-to-back games against the Wizards after a 31 point game against the Lakers.  The Pistons will have a tough decision to make when Jalen Duren returns as they probably should continue to start Jenkins, but Duren doesn’t bring the same level of spacing as John Collins does and John Collins was signed to complement Jalen Duren at the four.

But, those are the good problems to have when you have a team as deep as the Pistons.

Another player to watch for the Pelicans is Jeremiah Fears, who had a triple-double in the Pelicans’ dismantling of the Golden State Warriors on Monday.  He is starting to put things together and develop into their future at point guard right at a time when Dejounte Murray has requested a trade.  Say what you want about the process in how the Pelicans have drafted and acquired picks in the last couple seasons, but they at least appear to have hit on Fears.

Another reclamation project they have hit on is former Piston, Saddiq Bey.  He earned an extension in the offseason after putting together a pretty solid season last year after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered a couple years ago.  As Pistons fans know, Bey is capable of getting hot, so he is another player they will have to look out for.

Overall, this shouldn’t be too difficult of a matchup for the Pistons, but after the emotions of a hard-fought battle last night, I would not be shocked to see a slow start out of the Pistons.  But, even with the injured players, the Pistons are the more talented team and should be able to win this game.

Lineups

Detroit Pistons (9-4):  Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Heurter, Ausar Thompson, John Collins

New Orleans Pelicans (5-10):  Jeremiah Fears, Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey, Zion Williamson, Yves Missi

SAN ANTONIO, TX - NOVEMBER 17: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons drives to the basket during the game against the San Antonio Spurs on November 17, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

The Detroit Pistons played their best defensive game of the year to overwhelm the San Antonio Spurs en route to a 105-93 win in San Antonio. For the Pistons, it was a true return to the identity that has defined them during the JB Bickerstaff era. Play suffocating defense, never quit on any play, and attack the paint.

Some of those qualities have been absent this year with the loss of Jalen Duren down low. Combine that with going against the hottest team in the NBA with the most dominant big man since Shaquille O’Neal, and it seemed like a recipe for trouble.

Of course, what we should have all learned by now is that the moment you count out the Detroit Pistons is the moment they deliver their best performances.

The Pistons were led by a dominant back court of Cade Cunningham, the NBA superstar, and Daniss Jenkins, the most dangerous man in the first year of a real NBA contract after cutting his teeth in the G League. Cunningham scored 27 points and added six assists. Jenkins added 25 points and five assists.

They needed to deliver big time because the Pistons’ roster was depleted even more than normal. Detroit was not only without Duren down low, but they were also without their two most dangerous 3-point threats in Duncan Robinson and Isaiah Joe, and without one of the best defenders off the bench in the NBA, Ron Holland.

That didn’t matter, because every player on the Pistons roster understood how big this game was, and that if you want to call yourself an NBA title contender, you have to bring it against a powerhouse like the Spurs.

San Antonio entered tonight averaging 118.8 points per game, and before tonight, its lowest output of the season was 104 points against the Oklahoma City Thunder. To hold this Spurs team to more than 10 points below their previous low is a statement to the rest of the NBA. The Detroit Pistons can beat anyone on any night.

And anyone can be the hero. Paul Reed hit some huge acrobatic shots down low. Ausar Thompson almost had his second triple-double of November with 14 points, 12 assists, and nine rebounds. Thompson was matched up with Wembenyama on the night so that Wemby could play a roaming free safety. Detroit counteracted that by putting the ball in Ausar’s hands and using him a lot in pick-and-roll situations. Thompson was attacking early and finding open teammates throughout the night.

The Pistons outscored the Spurs in the paint 60-44 and in fast-break points 24-15. San Antonio is the lowest-turnover team in the NBA, but the Pistons were able to ratchet up the pressure, fight through screens, deflect handoffs and entry passes, and generate 10 steals. It was a total team effort from one of the best teams in the NBA.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs Spurs preview: No Duncan or Duren, others must step up
pistons.body:
The Detroit Pistons are down four rotation players as they match up with Tobias Harris and the San Antonio Spurs. Harris has not made his season debut due to a nagging calf injury. That hasn’t affected the Spurs in the slightest.

The absences of Duncan Robinson, Ron Holland, Isaiah Joe, and Jalen Duren surely make a difference for Detroit. The shooters will be extremely missed, with Victor Wembanyama’s presence shrinking the floor.

Duren has some eye-popping moments against the MVP candidate, but we won’t see that big man clash until late March, unless they line it up in the NBA cup Finals.

Jalen Duren dunks all over Wemby 😳 pic.twitter.com/zVaRSeZ4Ca
— Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) February 24, 2026

GAME VITALS

Where: Frost Bank Center, San Antonio, TX

When: 8 PM EST

Watch: Peacock NBC

Odds: Pistons (+9.5)

There aren’t too many games where Cade Cunningham doesn’t step on the floor as the guy. He can be him in any matchup, but it will take a lot to top Wemby. Considering how small Detroit is currently, their hands are full with the 7-foot-4 Frenchman.

John Collins started at the 5 over the last three games. With Robinson out, don’t be surprised if Paul Reed re-enters the starting group. That isn’t a Goliath pairing, but some teams opt for as much size as possible when defending Wemby.

The “put the small on Wemby” philosophy hasn’t been fruitful this year. Wemby is dunking everything. Per Basketball-Reference, 27 percent of his shots are slams. That’s way up from 18 percent last year. Detroit could have success “forcing” him to shoot. He’s shooting 32 percent on triples and 39 percent on all middies.

That’s a tough ask. Detroit’s defense came up short against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat Saturday night. Giannis scored 24 points in the paint. That same type of shots-at-the-rim challenge is up tonight.

Here’s a glass-half-full takeaway from Collins. He’s made at least two 3s in each of the past three games. Yes, glass half full for sure. Plus, he is shooting 38 percent from 3 on the season. Teams haven’t cared, though. They still treat him like a maybe shooter. San Antonio will absolutely dare him to shoot from the wings tonight.

Detroit needs the open ones. Collins has to start hitting enough for teams to feel they need to stay attached. The defensive rotations can get better. The rim protection will not get better. That’s not who he is. He’s been disappointing defensively and on the glass. The shooting has to be feared enough to aid the spacing — high percentages on low volume won’t shift defenses.

The Spurs are the second-best defense in the league, only trailing the Minnesota Timberwolves. While Wemby suffocates you, the “smalls” relentlessly hound.

Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper are big guards who get after it. Castle especially is an All-Defense caliber guy. Cade plays to win, but he’ll want to let loose against Castle, who gave him trouble in the second February game last year.

Cade was better in the first one and led Detroit to the dub. He’ll try to do that again tonight with an undermanned roster.

Ausar Thompson will do some leading too, as he’s had the ball in his hands a lot more. According to Databallr, here’s his on-ball percentage by year:

2024: 9.3%

2025: 14.4%

2026: 17.6%

2027: 21.2%

Ausar got his first triple-double a few games ago. He was so involved, zipping up and down the floor. Detroit needs all of that and then some tonight. He has to stay on the floor.

In the dawg category, Daniss Jenkins is in the 100th percentile. He steps up whenever Detroit is counted out. No Robinson, so he’ll surely start. The Spurs don’t allow many 3s, so Jenkins needs to be ready to knock down when he gets his chances.

Jenkins creates a lot of chances with his I don’t care who’s guarding me mentality, so expect him to get them up, with the paint being limited.

You can’t fault his philosophy either. Jenkins is shooting 42 percent on five 3s a game. He makes them count. Detroit will need every ounce of his fearlessness as they travel to San Antonio. The Spurs are winners of 12 in a row. Detroit will rarely be nine-point underdogs. Let’s see how they come out in this position.

Projected starting lineup

Detroit Pistons (8-4): Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Ausar Thompson, John Collins, Paul Reed

San Antonio Spurs (12-2): De’Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell, Victor Wembanyama

Who or what has been the most impressive in the No-Duren stretch?

pistons.headline: 3-man Fastbreak: Navigating without Duren
pistons.body:
DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 04: Jalen Duren #0 of the Detroit Pistons looks on from the bench during a game against the Philadelphia 76ers at Little Caesars Arena on November 04, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Sitting at 8-4, Detroit finds itself right under Boston and Philadelphia at the top of the conference – having already knocked off both squads. What makes that start even more impressive is how much of it has come with Jalen Duren sidelined by a hamstring issue.

It shouldn’t come as a shock to see the Pistons maintaining their place among the Eastern Conference elite, but the bigger story might be how long it takes the rest of the field to gel. Contenders like Indiana, Orlando, and Toronto entered the campaign with big ambitions, yet all three are currently stumbling below .500.

Here are a few key takeaways from this recent run of action.

1. Has the team’s limitations from last season changed?

Fresh off a impressive 60-win campaign, Detroit has quieted critics who viewed their summer moves with skepticism. Retaining their core talent with long-term deals has paid immediate dividends, as their roster continuity continues to fuel early momentum.

While the Pistons have routinely handled lesser opponents, their battles against heavyweights like New York, Philadelphia, and Los Angeles revealed familiar flaws. During offensive droughts, the ball movement stalled, resulting in over-reliance on Cade Cunningham to create individual magic while the surrounding unit remained static.

Is it a real cause for concern yet considering they’ve been down their second best player? Not in the short term.

This foundational identity guarantees postseason basketball and likely home-court advantage, yet doubts regarding their ceiling remain. Rumors of offseason trade pursuits suggest the front office recognizes the missing piece, but until a major acquisition materializes, lingering questions about their championship credentials will remain.

2. Inside -> out offense

Detroit’s identity remains largely unchanged from the past two seasons, but the offense is clearly evolving, especially without their All-NBA big man.

Last season, Detroit led the league with 57.9 points in the paint per game. This year, that figure has fallen to 47.2, around the middle of the pack. Duren’s absence since the second game has certainly played a role, but the shift also reflects the team’s offseason moves. Detroit moved on from Isaiah Stewart and Tobias Harris while adding better floor spacers in John Collins and Isaiah Jones. Duncan Robinson has also taken on a larger role, posting career highs with 17.4 points per game while shooting 43.1% from three.

That improved spacing has helped fuel Detroit’s early success, but defense remains the team’s foundation, with Detroit still leading the league in several defensive categories. Once Duren returns, it will be worth watching whether the offensive approach changes.

3. Dannis’s development

In the three games since Jenkins replaced Paul Reed in the starting lineup on November 8, Jenkins averaged 24.7 points, 5.7 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 2.3 steals and 4.3 three-pointers per game. The undrafted guard made occasional starts last season, but only when Cunningham was injured or resting. This year, the temporary promotion while Duren remains out shows that J.B. Bickerstaff trusts Jenkins with a larger role.

Since emerging in Detroit last season, Jenkins has gone from a promising two-way player to a legitimate contributor on a contending team. Jenkins has also shown a willingness to embrace any role and play with maximum effort. The question is no longer whether Jenkins can be a reliable role player, but how large that role can become as the stakes rise.

At 25, Jenkins still has room to grow. He is shooting 42.4% from three this season on 4.9 attempts per game and is averaging fewer turnovers than last year despite playing eight more minutes per night.

That chip on the shoulder may be Jenkins’ greatest strength, and continued growth could be an underrated factor in how far the Pistons go this season.

pistons.headline: Pistons vs. Wizards final score: Cade makes history in double OT win
pistons.body:
WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 12: Cade Cunningham #2 of the Detroit Pistons celebrates against the Washington Wizards during the first overtime at Capital One Arena on November 12, 2026 in Washington, DC. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images

Cade Cunningham scored a career-high 52 points, and the Detroit Pistons needed every single one of them in a 144-140 victory in double overtime against the Washington Wizards. It was not just a career-best night for Cunningham, not just one of the top-5 scoring performances in Pistons history, it was the first game in NBA history that saw a player score 50 points, dish 11 assists, and commit zero turnovers.

Cunningham simply did it all. He scored 30 points in the fourth quarter and overtime. That includes a critical 3-pointer after the Wizards had crawled their way back into the lead in the first overtime on an Anthony Davis alley-oop dunk.

The Pistons trailed 130-127 and each team had traded misses. Cunningham calmly took the ball up the left side of the floor, took a pass from Ausar Thompson, and walked into a movement 3-pointer that hit nothing but net to tie the game. On the next possession, Cade swung the ball to Duncan Robinson for what felt like a game-sealing 3 with 9 seconds left, but a video review determined Duncan had approximately 1 milimeter of his foot on the line and changed it to a two.

The scoring barrage also included critical stretch in the fourth quarter where he scored eight points and assisted another to account for 11 of Detroit’s final 12 points of the fourth quarter. Cunningham also locked up Trae Young on defense with Detroit up 119-118 in the final 30 seconds of the fourth. He forced Young into the sideline, cut off any passing lane, deflected the ball, and forced shot clock violation.

Sadly, after Cade hit two free throws to make it a 3-point game, Young redeemed himself by hitting an off-balance three from 29 feet away to give us our two overtimes of fun.

The Detroit Lions (7-2) are back home in Week 11 and preparing to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6). As the Lions work to reacclimate after returning from Germany earlier in the week, they elected to hold a walkthrough on Wednesday.

A walkthrough practice means that all participation levels are estimates from the coaching staff based on how the player would have participated in a traditional practice. So, with that in mind, let’s look at Wednesday’s injury report and get you up to date on what we know.

Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded.

Injured list updates

RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December

OL Giovanni Manu (undisclosed, NFI) — eligible to begin practicing at any time

OL Ben Bartch (foot, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time

EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL, IR) — requires surgery; his season is over

LB Devin White (forearm, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time

LB Jack Campbell (neck, IR) — determined to play football again

S Thomas Harper (ankle, IR) — eligible to begin practicing at any time

Estimated no practice

C Cade Mays (low ankle sprain)

Earlier in the week, Lions coach Dan Campbell said he wasn’t sure if Mays would be able to return to play this week, and while an estimated no practice to start the week is not ideal, he could still return to practice this week, even if the plan is not to play him.

Estimated limited practice

RB Sione Vaki (ankle)

DL Tyler Lacy (shoulder) — New Injury

LB Joe Bachie (knee) — New Injury

CB D.J. Reed (hip) — UPGRADED from no practice last week

CB Khalil Dorsey (ankle) — New Injury

CB Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) — New Injury

Vaki missed two practices last week with an ankle injury, returned to practice on Friday in Germany, and played in the game. An estimated limited practice is a step in the right direction as he looks to stay on the field this weekend.

Lacy did not appear to be limited by this injury in Germany, and Campbell has noted that the big end is in the plans to help replace Hutchinson, so an estimated limited practice is worth monitoring but with some optimism.

Bachie didn’t play many defensive snaps last Sunday, but he’s been a consistent special teams contributor. Hopefully this injury won’t keep him sidelined.

Reed’s status is still up in the air, as Campbell said he wasn’t sure whether the Lions’ top corner would be available against the Bucs. That being said, an estimated limited practice is a good sign that even if he can’t return this Sunday, he could be on track to return against the Bears on Thanksgiving.

Dorsey was notably injured against the Patriots and required trainers’ assistance on the field in Germany. The Lions never assigned him an in-game injury designation, which suggests they were trying to see if he could return. Couple that with an estimated limited practice, and he’ll have a chance to play on Sunday.

Rakestraw played only a limited number of snaps in Germany, though it’s not clear whether that was the plan ahead of time or whether this shoulder injury changed things. We’ll have to see how he progresses this week before we know his availability.

Estimated full practice

S Kerby Joseph (knee)

Joseph has officially been activated from the PUP list, and while his knee is still being monitored, he is expected to return to the starting lineup this Sunday against the Bucs.

“Barring anything else here negatively—which there hasn’t been, he’s progressed nicely here—the plan would be to get him going this week. Get him going and get him into Tampa Bay and let him play,” Campbell said.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions officially activate Kerby Joseph, place Aidan Hutchinson on IR
lions.body:
DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 28: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31) takes the field prior to the Detroit Lions versus the Cleveland Browns game on Sunday September 28, 2025 at Ford Field in Detroit, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

On Wednesday, the Detroit Lions made two moves that were both expected, placing Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve, while activating Kerby Joseph from the Physically Unable to Perform list to the 53-man roster. Joseph takes Hutchinson’s spot on the roster, keeping the roster at 53 players for now.

Hutchinson’s placement on injured reserve is no surprise, given that the team confirmed he tore his ACL while celebrating in Sunday’s win over the New England Patriots. While Hutchinson will miss the remainder of the season, coach Dan Campbell was optimistic he’d work his way back and be better than ever next year.

“Knowing Hutch, he will attack this like he did the last time, and he will come back better than ever next year,” Campbell said.

He also mentioned that the damage in his knee may go beyond just his ACL.

“It sounds like there’s a little bit (more damage) in there. I don’t know how significant all of that is. And some of it you’re not going to know until you go in there and actually do the procedure,” Campbell said.

As for Joseph, Campbell already notified media earlier in the week that the plan was to get the All-Pro safety involved this week. And while Joseph will be on a pitch count against the Buccaneers, Campbell doesn’t expect it to be too strict.

“Is there a pitch count? Yeah, but not like what (Brian) Branch had his first game. So, I think we’re going to be able to get a little bit more out of Kerby here,” Campbell said on Tuesday.

In addition to these moves, the Lions also re-signed cornerback Nick Whiteside to the practice squad, filling the vacancy left by Detroit’s cutting of defensive lineman Ben Stille earlier this week.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions planning to debut Ahmed Hassanein vs. Buccaneers
lions.body:
CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 13: Detroit Lions defensive end Ahmed Hassanein (99) walks off the field at halftime during the preseason game between the Detroit Lions and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images

The long wait is over.

Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell noted on Wednesday that the current plan is to have defensive end—and fan favorite—Ahmed Hassanein make his NFL debut this Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Hassanein has been a healthy scratch all season, despite the fact that he was one of the more impressive defensive players during training camp and the preseason, albeit mostly working with the second and third teams. But after Aidan Hutchinson’s season-ending ACL injury last week, Campbell mentioned Hassanein among the players he has confidence in at the edge position moving forward.

“We still feel pretty good about the edges that we have with (DJ) Wonnum and Derrick Moore and (Eric) O’Neill, and then we’ll probably get Ahmed going here a little bit,” Campbell said.

Campbell was then asked how ready he thinks Hassanein will be to finally play in his first regular-season action.

“How ready do you think he’s going to be?” Campbell said with a smirk, referencing Hassanein’s unmatchable intensity and drive.

“He brings it every day in practice, just like you saw in camp,” Campbell said. “He’s out there and he tries do—everything you ask him to do in practice as far as he’s working his craft, what he’s being taught to by (DL coach) Kacey (Rodgers). And then when you get him on scout team, he wants to do exactly what the opponent does. […] He’s making himself better; he makes us better. So it’s going to be a great opportunity.”

Hassanein was the Lions’ sixth-round pick in 2025, and lost most of his rookie season to a pectoral injury before rejoining the practice squad late. Due to his unique origin story—hailing from Egypt and learning the game of football late in high school—and intensity (telling Campbell “I will die for you” on his draft day phone call), Hassanein quickly became a fan favorite. And he flashed some of that football potential in the preseason, when he tallied 2.0 sacks, five quarterback hits, and one forced fumble in three games.

With him—along with the versatility of players like Tyler Lacy, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Levi Onwuzurike—Campbell believes the team will be ready to bounce back from the Hutchinson injury, no matter what the situation calls for.

“I feel like we’re equipped to kinda play the game any way we need to defensively with what we’ve got,” Campbell said.

lions.headline: Lions vs. Buccaneers thoughts after watching TB vs. Bears
lions.body:
CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers carries the ball against the Chicago Bears during the third quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are coming off a bye after a narrow loss to the Chicago Bears on “Sunday Night Football.”

To get a sense of what the Detroit Lions could expect from the Buccaneers this week, I went back and re-watched that Buccaneers vs. Bears game and came out with six thoughts about this upcoming matchup.

Pass rush very effective… when blitzing

The Buccaneers were an absolute terror for Caleb Williams, forcing him into four interceptions and just a 59.5 completion percentage. And while they only sacked him once, Williams faced a total of 25 pressures.

But the Buccaneers also had to be super aggressive to create that pressure. Per NFL Pro, they blitzed 63.4% of the time, second only to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9. Turns out for the season, they absolutely need to blitz to create pressure. For the season, the Bucs only have a 33.2% pressure rate (24th) and 5.0% sack rate (25th). But they may have found some answers with the blitz this past game.

For the season, they still look like an ineffective blitzing team (28th in pressure rate when blitzing, 30th in sack rate), but with their highest blitz rate of the season vs. the Bears, they got home early and often.

Bucky Irving is a dude

Irving finished this game with 97 rushing yards, 4.9 yards per carry, and two touchdowns, but it was the manner in which he gained those yards that was particularly impressive. Per NFL Pro, he had 83 yards after contract.

For the season, Irving ranks fifth in rushing yards after contact per game (65.9), 12th in yards after contract per rush (3.6), and leads the league with 16 broken tackles forced.

He is a forced to be reckoned with, and the Lions will need to make sure they are tackling by committee on Sunday.

The Bucs run game is inconsistent but strong

No one runs the ball more than Tampa Bay, although that is admittedly skewed by Week 8, when Tampa ran the ball 56 times and threw it just three times in a monsoon.

Still, I was mesmerized by just how versatile and diverse their run game was. They do under center, shotgun, zone, power, gap. They’ll try to run between the tackles, then hit you with a toss play. This graph is a pretty good indication of how they aren’t married to one kind of run, which speaks to the versatility of their decent offensive line (top-10 per PFF):

Every team's run concept mix through Week 10: pic.twitter.com/5cK0tUTnge
— SūmerSports (@SumerSports) November 17, 2026

But despite their strong running back and diverse scheme, the efficiency just isn’t what it should be. They’re ninth in rush EPA and ninth in success rate (43.9%). That’s certainly not bad, but it just seems like it should be better.

Passing game has no identity

Against the Bears, Baker Mayfield was just bad. He was inaccurate (-7.9% completion over expected) and he threw two interception. Aside from one deep ball connection with Tez Johnson, just about everything he completed was within 5 yards of the line of scrimmage.

He hasn’t been helped by a weak receiving corps. While Emeka Egbuka still has WR1 potential, the Buccaneers were victimized by a pair of critical drops from second-year receiver Johnson. In short, it just looked like there was no chemistry between Mayfield and his receivers.

For the season, the Buccaneers are just 30th in dropback EPA and 31st in dropback success rate. They could play Jalon Daniels this week, but he’s averaging just 5.1 yard sper attempt and has a 63.3 passer rating on the season.

Interior offensive line could be a weakness

With Jeffery Simmons aboard, the Bears were able to create a ton of havoc up the middle vs. Tampa, in both the run and in terms of pass rush. While at times it seems like Tampa is getting a ton of push up the middle, all three starting interior offensive linemen rank in the bottom half of the league in run blocking grade.

Pass protection seemed like a bigger issue against the Bears, though. All three posted PFF pass blocking grades lower than 60, with left guard Ben Bredeson ceding pressure, center Graham Barton responsible for one sack, and right guard Cody Mauch posting a 52.1 pass blocking grade.

While Detroit may be overmatched at the tackle positions—with Tristan Wirfs and Jake Goedeke at the top of their games, and Aidan Hutchinson out—Alim McNeill, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Tyleik Williams could be in line for big days.

That secondary is balling

While they were helped by a reinvigorated pass rush against the Bears, the secondary made everything difficult for Caleb Williams on Sunday night.

Jacob Parrish is perhaps the most surprising of breakout players, as he is currently PFF’s No.4 graded cornerback in just his second year in the NFL. Opposite him, Zyon McCollum has 11 pass breakups (t-third in NFL) and four interceptions (t-third). And Tampa’s safeties Antoine Winfield Jr. and Tykee Smith are both ballers, as well.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions’ playoff odds: Postseason, division, Super Bowl probabilities
lions.body:
Munich, Germany - November 15: Jared Goff of Detroit Lions gestures during the NFL match between New England Patriots and Detroit Lions at Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Mario Hommes/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images

The Detroit Lions are in a pretty darn good position through 10 weeks, sitting at 7-2 overall while currently holding the NFC’s No. 2 seed. They’re at the top of a competitive NFC North via tiebreakers, and you can see the full NFC playoff picture laid out here.

But despite that 7-2 record, the Lions’ path to the playoffs will not be a cakewalk in the final eight weeks of the season. Not only do they have four remaining divisional games, but the entire NFC conference is pretty competitive among the top-nine teams. For example, the ninth-ranked team in the conference—the Los Angeles Rams—are just two games behind Detroit at 6-4, and LA has won four in a row. The 6-4 Seattle Seahawks (eighth in NFC) have won three of their last four.

So let’s take our first look at the Lions’ playoff odds—including their chances to win the NFC North, secure the conference’s top seed, and reach the Super Bowl—according to several analytical models.

Postseason odds:

NYT simulator: 79%
RBSDM: 78%
DVOA: 77.7%
ESPN (FPI): 89.4%

To hold a 7-2 record and have less than a four-in-five probability to make the playoffs shows just how competitive this division is. However, you’ll notice a pattern here: ESPN is curiously very high on the Lions compared to the rest of the models. I’m not exactly clear why, but I imagine it has something to do with having just the 16th-hardest remaining schedule, per their model. That’s among the easiest compared to the rest of the NFC contenders (49ers: 9th, Rams: 1st, Bears: 6th, Seahawks: 2nd, Vikings: 22nd, Packers: 5th).

NFC North title odds

NYT simulator: 24% (Behind Vikings, Bears)
RBSDM: 26% (Behind Vikings, Bears)
DVOA: 19.4% (Behind Vikings, Bears)
ESPN (FPI): 33.1% (Behind Vikings)

For all four models, the Vikings have the best odds to win the division, despite Detroit currently holding the top spot. Perhaps that’s because of their schedule. Perhaps that’s because they’ve already tallied an impressive 3-1 record in the division.

The Bears are generally favored over Detroit as the stronger of the two teams, but they’ll have to overcome a brutal schedule ahead—and an o-2 record in the division. Meanwhile, every model has the Packers’ NFC North title odds below 3 percent, because they’re both two games back and have a 1-3 divisional record.

NFC’s No. 1 seed

NYT simulator: 10%
RBSDM: 12%
DVOA: 6.9%
ESPN: 9%

Though Detroit is just a single game behind the NFC West-leading 49ers—and San Francisco has a brutal schedule—Detroit has somewhere around just a 10 percent chance of earning a first round bye. But given the bye didn’t help the Lions at all in 2024, I doubt Detroit fans care much.

Super Bowl appearance odds

ESPN (FPI): 10.4%
DVOA: 5.9%

Yes, it’s weird to me, too, that ESPN gives the Lions a better shot to make it to the Super Bowl than to win the NFC’s top regular season seed. But I’ll take a 10.4% chance at this point in the season.

DVOA is much more down on Detroit, seeing as they have the Lions ranked as the 13th best team overall.

lions.headline: Detroit Lions scouting report: Tampa Bay’s defense is dangerous
lions.body:
CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Alex Anzalone #34 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers reacts during the third quarter against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images

After a trip overseas to Germany, the Detroit Lions return home to Ford Field to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Detroit comes in at 7-2, on a five-game winning streak with no signs of slowing down, and has become the top team in the NFC North. Both sides of the ball are humming, despite being down star EDGE Aidan Hutchinson for the season with a torn ACL.

Tampa Bay, meanwhile, is coming off a much-needed bye week after winning two of its last three games to improve to 3-6. While the record isn’t pretty, this team is better than it shows. They were without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for three weeks, and the team went 1-2 in his absence. Since he’s been back, the offense has improved, and the defense continues to play strong. Like Detroit, the Bucs still have a chance to win their division despite their record, as the NFC South continues to appear as the worst division in the NFL.

Let’s take a deep look at the Bucs and how their 2026 season has been so far.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers

2026 season thus far (3-6)

Week 1: Lost to Cincinnati Bengals 33-27
Week 2: Lost to Cleveland Browns 23-19
Week 3: Lost to Minnesota Vikings 23-16
Week 4: Lost to Green Bay Packers 17-14
Week 5: Defeated Dallas Cowboys 24-16
Week 6: Lost to Pittsburgh Steelers 26-19 OT
Week 7: Defeated Carolina Panthers 43-13
Week 8: Defeated Atlanta Falcons 16-0
Week 9: Lost to Chicago Bears 27-24
Week 10: BYE

Offensive stats:

As I mentioned earlier, Mayfield has missed time due to injury, and he hasn’t been as solid as he was last year, throwing for 922 yards, a 60.6 completion percentage, three touchdowns, and four interceptions. This follows a contract extension he signed with the Bucs for three years at $165 million. In his absence, backup rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels took over and was a mixed bag, throwing for 501 yards, a 61.2 completion percentage, three touchdowns, and five interceptions in the four games he played for Mayfield.

While the passing game has had its woes, the running back spot has seen solid play from its starter, Bucky Irving. Irving has been having a solid season, rushing for 825 yards (fifth in the NFL), averaging 4.9 yards per carry and seven touchdowns. When the team needed to lean on him, he’s answered the call as the passing game has taken a step back.

The wide receiver room seemed to have found its next star in Emeka Egbuka last year, but now that their other former star, Mike Evans, is gone, it’s been a rough go for the group. Egbuka is the leader with 31 catches for 278 yards and two touchdowns, but for the leader to be that low at Week 11 is shocking. Chris Godwin just doesn’t look like the same player he was before the injuries piled up, with 29 catches for 259 yards. The team has a young core outside of Godwin, and life without Evans has been rougher than expected.

Tampa Bay just can’t seem to move the ball through the air, as they are in the bottom tier of multiple passing statistics. Part of the issue has been the quarterback play, but also the receivers struggling to get open. According to PFF, Tampa Bay’s receivers grade out to 59.2, ranked 31st, ahead of only the Los Angeles Chargers. The offensive line is ranked sixth in pass-blocking (73.7), so the blame can’t be put on them.

Defensive stats:

On defense, they’re one of the best units in the NFL, arguably better than the Minnesota Vikings. The pass rush isn’t as dominant, but it’s still a respectable front seven that teams can’t ignore. Linebacker David Walker leads the team with four sacks, with YaYa Diaby behind him at three. The former Lion trio of defenders—Al-Quadin Muhammad, Alex Anzalone, and A’Shawn Robinson—has four sacks combined. You also can’t ignore the beast at nose tackle, Vita Vea, who hasn’t had a big season, but is still a problem teams need to prepare for.

Meanwhile, the secondary has played solid defense this year. Cornerback Zyon McCollum is tied with Anzalone with four interceptions and seems to be becoming a lockdown corner for this team. Second-year cornerback Jacob Parrish has been involved too, leading the team in pass deflections with 14 and has two interceptions of his own.

This defense has dominated the turnover battle, with 21 takeaways, leading the NFL. They’ve gotten 16 interceptions and five fumbles. The entire defense picking off quarterbacks. It doesn’t matter where you throw the ball; anybody at any level can create a turnover through the air.

You also have to respect the Bucs’ run defense. They’ve allowed the fewest rushing yards (712) and the third-lowest yards per carry (3.5), while only allowing three rushing touchdowns, the fewest in the NFL. They’ve contained the big plays, allowing only four 20+ yard runs, with the longest being for 31.

Injury notes

Key players ruled out: None
Key players to monitor: QB Baker Mayfield (foot), WR Jalen McMillan (IR), WR Emeka Egbuka (foot), LB Yaya Diaby (knee)

Wide receiver Jalen McMillan is on IR and can return, but odds are, with no practices in him yet, he will not play this week. Egbuka was questionable in Week 9 but played with a foot injury, so with the week off, we can see if there has been any improvement. Diaby didn’t play in Week 9 due to a knee injury, so like Egbuka, if the week off helps, Diaby could return on Sunday.

The biggest story came up on Sunday: Mayfield suffered a foot injury against the Chicago Bears in Week 9, and his status this week is unknown. The Bucs signed quarterback Cooper Rush to their practice squad and elevated Easton Stick to their 53-man roster on Monday, which could be insurance if Mayfield can’t see the field on Sunday. Mayfield will be the biggest name to watch this week, and this team has played without him already this season, so it wouldn’t be something they haven’t dealt with before.

The #Lions are up big in Germany right now then head back to Detroit to face the #Buccaneers.

Right now, it’s unclear whether they’ll see Baker Mayfield, as sources say he’s dealing with a lower-leg injury suffered against the #Bears https://t.co/PJvIgW0idw
— Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 15, 2026

Biggest strength: Turnovers

You’d think with the amount of turnovers the Bucs defense has generated this year, their record would be better than what it is. Unfortunately, even if you lead the NFL in turnovers, it doesn’t always guarantee success. Either way, what the Bucs are doing right now is impressive, and even more impressive is how versatile they are in generating these interceptions.

Interceptions by position
Cornerbacks – 6
Linebackers – 6
Safeties – 2
Defensive lineman – 2

View Link

For a defensive lineman like Robinson to have as many interceptions as safety Tykee Smith is impressive. The Bucs are averaging 1.7 interceptions a game this season, and if they keep that pace up, they will finish with 30 interceptions. The last team to get 30 interceptions was the 2009 Green Bay Packers. While it isn’t close to the NFL record (hello 1961 San Diego Chargers with 49!), it’s still tough, and teams have to watch it when throwing the football.

Biggest weakness: Wide receivers

It’s a bit surprising to list this position as the team’s biggest weakness, but the evidence speaks for itself. The loss of Evans is bigger than the team expected, and while Egbuka is a good player to take on that WR1 role, he isn’t the same player as Evans. Egbuka had almost 1,000 yards last year as the number two option, but now that all eyes are on him, he isn’t getting that same kind of production. He certainly took advantage of having someone like Evans on the roster, but with most of the pressure on him, Egbuka seems to be struggling a little bit.

Then you have Godwin, who’s taken a big step back due to all the injuries that have piled up over the past few seasons. He hasn’t played a full season since 2023, and his production keeps going down, getting 576 yards in 2024, to 360 in 2025; he’s at 259 currently, and if he can stay healthy, he can do better than last year, but I am unsure about upending 2024’s numbers. Godwin still has talent; his body is just starting to take a toll from all the leg injuries that have slowed him down.

The depth behind those two isn’t much: second-year player Tez Johnson has 254 yards and one touchdown on only 11 catches, while third-round rookie Ted Hurst has 168 yards and a touchdown on 11 catches. Then you have McMillan hurt and third-year Kameron Johnson with only a catch for 3 yards. This room lacks depth; it’s top-loaded with Egbuka and Godwin, and with Godwin already missing three games, this young group is expected to do a lot of heavy lifting.

Key matchup: Lions ground attack vs. Buccaneers run defense

In back-to-back games, Detroit’s running attack will determine how the game goes. New England had a strong front, but Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs averaged 7.0 yards a carry, rushing for 153 yards and two touchdowns. This week, the challenge gets tougher, with Tampa Bay arguably having the best run defense in the NFL. Detroit needs the run to complement the pass, and it will need another strong game by Gibbs and backup running back Sione Vaki.

Detroit has an offense that can thankfully air it out to force defenses to worry less about Gibbs and more about quarterback Jared Goff and company. The problem this week is that Tampa Bay’s defense has been stellar, so if the passing attack can’t move it, Gibbs will have to carry the load. If Gibbs struggles as well, this game could go south for Detroit as they try to extend their winning streak to six games.

The Lions are coming back from Germany, so jet lag could be an excuse, but with their leader in head coach Dan Campbell, we know they won’t make any excuses. Detroit must run the ball successfully and keep it in Gibbs’ hands, as the Bucs are producing turnovers left and right this season.

Vegas line for Sunday: Lions favored by 7.5

lions.headline: Detroit Lions create practice squad spot, set stage for Wednesday roster moves
lions.body:
CINCINNATI, OHIO - AUGUST 13: Ben Stille #72 of the Detroit Lions walks off the field following the preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The Detroit Lions announced on Tuesday that they’ve released defensive lineman Ben Stille from the practice squad, creating a vacancy on the 17-man squad ahead of their week of preparation for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Stille, a 29-year-old veteran defensive lineman, was a standout during training camp this offseason, but he failed to make the 53-man roster. He was quickly signed to the practice squad and got the call-up for Detroit’s Week 1 game, playing just nine defensive snaps.

This move sets the stage for what will likely be a few roster moves on Wednesday. How the Lions will fill the practice squad spot remains to be seen, but it is certainly worth noting that on Monday, the Lions waived cornerback Nick Whiteside to make room for waiver claim DE Tyrus Wheat. On Tuesday, Whiteside cleared waivers, so if Detroit wanted to bring Whiteside back, there’s now a spot on the practice squad for that. Whiteside spent two months on the Lions’ practice squad earlier this year.

On top of that, the Lions are expected to activate safety Kerby Joseph from the Physically Unable to Perform list to the 53-man roster on Wednesday, the final day of Joseph’s 21-day evaluation window. If the Lions don’t activate Joseph, he would be shut down for the year, but on Tuesday, coach Dan Campbell indicated that Joseph will not only be activated, but they expect him to have a significant role in Sunday’s game against the Buccaneers.

“The plan is to get him going. I think we’re going to let him play,” Campbell said.

It’s not clear how the Lions will create the roster spot for Joseph, but the easiest way would be to place Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve after he suffered a torn ACL on Sunday.

lions.headline: Lions vs. Patriots Song of the Game: ‘Time’ by Pink Floyd
lions.body:
MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions goes down with an injury while celebrating getting a sack during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images

The international excursion is officially over. The Detroit Lions return home from their trip to Germany with a better record than they left the States with, but it came at a cost. Will it end up costing them their season? Will they rally in the same way they did a couple of seasons ago?

Only time will tell.

Lions vs. Patriots Week 10 Song of the Game: “Time” by Pink Floyd

Ticking away the moments that make up a dull day
You fritter and waste the hours in an off-hand way
Kicking around on a piece of ground in your home town
Waiting for someone or something to show you the way

Getting this out of the way from the jump: big stock down for social media last week. Opting out of the scrolling experience was a wise choice, but it took a couple of days to realize why last week felt like such a slog and a bummer. Avoiding socials was the only cure for the intense FOMO brought on by people’s constant stream of posting their good ol’ time in Germany.

And if you made the trip, very happy for you—truly hope you had an unforgettable experience because it doesn’t get much more memorable than that, right? There’s no room to be envious, or else the overlords in this country are getting the exact kind of class dissension they want. For those who couldn’t make the trip, maybe one day you’ll be shown the way, financially, that affords you the opportunity to travel abroad and see the world and your football team in distant lands. Maybe one day you’ll be high enough up on the totem pole at your job and have the autonomy to leave your work and responsibilities behind for an entire week. There’s only one way to find out if you’ll get there, and it’s through; here’s to the next intercontinental trip.

Tired of lying in the sunshine, staying home to watch the rain
And you are young and life is long, and there is time to kill today
And then one day you find ten years have got behind you
No one told you when to run, you missed the starting gun

Aidan Hutchinson’s injury, one that’s going to put an end to his 2026 season, is a harrowing reminder of the Lions’ window with their current core. By the conclusion of this season, he’ll have missed 20 games over the last three seasons, and who knows how much of his 2027 season will be compromised by rehab and training. He’s no spring chicken anymore—Hutchinson will turn 27 before the start of next season—and the (freak) injuries have put a sizable dent in the prime of his promising career. The hope is he’ll bounce back from this setback just like the last time, but the runway is getting shorter, and the clock is ticking—for both Hutchinson and this current iteration of the Lions’ core.

2022 doesn’t feel too distant, but the NFL’s clock measures days differently, and injuries only exacerbate its passage of time. The defensive core of players signed to extensions—Hutchinson, Jack Campbell, Kerby Joseph, and Alim McNeill—rides on the hopes of Joseph’s knee and McNeill’s dominant (and entirely overlooked/under appreciated) season to keep the defense afloat for the rest of 2026.

Not trying to be a “miserable piece of shit,” not trying to ruin anyone’s day, just looking at things in a relative way.

Every year is getting shorter, never seem to find the time
Plans that either come to naught, or half a page of scribbled lines
Hanging on in quiet desperation is the English way
The time is gone, the song is over, thought I’d something more to say

Acknowledging the weight of Hutchinson’s absence isn’t an exercise in quiet desperation—it’s just the reality of how fragile things can be in the NFL. At 7-2, the Lions are still in the driver’s seat of their season, and we know Dan Campbell: the urgency inside Allen Park isn’t rooted in panic or desperation. The locker room’s perspective echoed a shared sentiment following Sunday’s win over New England:

“It’s completely different,” McNeill said of the defense’s situation compared to 2024. “We went, what, 15-2? So we had a good year. This d-line is different. This defense is a lot different. I feel like it’s equipped a lot different. Hutch is Hutch. We have the pieces, and the puzzle pieces to put in the game to try and create that production. But I think this is a way different equipped d-line.”

Hutchinson has faced the music, but this season isn’t over until the fat lady sings. McNeill and the rest of the defense still have something to say before anyone can write off the Detroit Lions.

If you want to relive previous Lions seasons, you can find the playlists we curated below: 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022. And if you want to read previous versions of our Song of the Game columns, you can find those here.

lions.headline: NFL Week 11 power rankings: Despite dominating win, Lions fall following Hutchinson injury
lions.body:
Nov 15, 2026; Munich, DEU; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell during the second quarter against the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The Detroit Lions (7-2) are riding a five-game win streak and are coming off a dominating 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany. Their offense is firing on all cylinders, their defense is improving (they’ve allowed just 12.8 points against per game over the last four games), and they currently sit atop the NFC North because they’re 2-0 in divisional games, ahead of the Vikings (7-2, 3-1 in division), Bears (7-2, 0-2), and Packers (6-4, 1-3).

While the Lions have been on an upward trajectory for over a month, they lost star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season in their last game, and the national media seems convinced it will be the Lions’ undoing.

Of the eight national power rankings we track, the Lions fell in five, stayed level in two, and climbed in just one. When comparing the Lions’ ranking to those within the division, the Lions land at third in all but one ranking, with the Bears ahead on every list and the Vikings ahead on all but CBS Sports, despite the Lions holding a head-to-head victory over them just three games ago.

So while the national pundits are dropping the Lions down their rankings and worrying over what could have been or where things go from here, Lions coach Dan Campbell refuses to discount this team despite their injury obstacles:

Great answer from Dan Campbell. pic.twitter.com/kf3jR7zqyF
— Colton Pouncy (@colton_pouncy) November 17, 2026

Let’s take a closer look at this week’s national power rankings.

NFL.com: 8 (Previous rank: 7)

From Nick Shook:

Detroit’s offense is among the most consistent units in the NFL — save for Week 9 — and the team continues to enjoy improvement from the defensive side. The Lions only fall this week because of movement around them, although I am quite concerned with how they’re going to replace Aidan Hutchinson’s production.

CBS Sports: 8 (Previous rank: 8)

From Pete Prisco:

The loss of Aidan Hutchinson with a knee injury could be a damning blow to this defense. The high-powered offense might need to score even more.

Sporting News: 8 (Previous rank: 10)

From Vinnie Iyer:

The Lions are up to a five-game winning streak after starting 2-2. Amon-Ra St. Brown’s monster game in Munich reminds that Jared Goff has fully embraced an aggressive wide receiver-centric offense. The simplicity of the production has them flying under the radar a little to other NFC contenders.

Sports Illustrated: 9 (Previous rank: 6)

From Connor Orr:

I hate to knock the Lions down after a convincing win over the Patriots, but losing Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson may be a bridge too far for this team to recover from. I think the Lions are still good enough to limp into the playoffs, but can this offense score at a historic rate to make up for all the attrition?

The Athletic: 9 (Previous rank: 8)

From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall:

Breakout player: Alim McNeill

The sixth-year defensive tackle already has a career high in sacks (6.5) and quarterback hits (11), and the Lions are going to need him more than ever with Aidan Hutchinson out due to injury. Detroit proved again Sunday that its offense is Super Bowl-worthy, but the defense is 28th in the league in defensive EPA (minus-5.2 per 100 snaps).

USA Today: 10 (Previous rank: 6)

From Nate Davis:

Barring another catastrophic injury, hard to envision a scenario where this team misses the playoffs. But it might be wise to begin conserving RB Jahmyr Gibbs’ touches, because he may need 30 per game in January if this team is going to make any kind of Super Bowl push.

ESPN: 10 (Previous rank: 10)

From ESPN Staff, excerpt from Eric Woodyard:

Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Jahmyr Gibbs

There’s a reason the Lions made Gibbs the NFL’s highest-paid running back over the offseason. And he has proved to be worth every penny after a phenomenal start to his fourth season as the team’s clear lead back. With 62 career touchdowns, the 24-year-old recently passed Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61) for the most through a player’s first four seasons in NFL history, per ESPN Research. His 1,384 scrimmage yards are the most a Lions player has produced through the first nine games of any season, and he has already scored 13 touchdowns.

Yahoo Sports: 11 (Previous rank: 9)

From Frank Schwab:

The Lions’ season changed with the reported ACL injury to defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. They were already without linebacker Jack Campbell, arguably the second-best player on the defense, and Detroit lost its unquestioned star because of a sack celebration. That’s brutal. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum are capable vets and will fill in, but they’re nowhere near Hutchinson’s level.

“Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy,” Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, according to NFL.com.

The Lions won on Sunday without Hutchinson for most of the game to improve to 7-2, and perhaps they have enough wins banked to make the playoffs in what will be a difficult wild-card race. But their hopes of being a Super Bowl contender are likely dashed without their two best defensive players.

michigan.headline: Hot Board 1.0
michigan.body:
Hot Board 1.0

Brian
November 18th, 2026 at 11:24 AM

Reports that Michigan is going to hire Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts for their open position are everywhere, resolving the "who can even fire Kyle Whittingham?" issue Michigan was staring down. Many of them note that Alberts has been ruthless when required, axing UNO football and Nebraska program legend Scott Frost in a couple of his previous AD stops. Business just picked up.
If—when, please—Alberts makes a move, this is what Michigan will be looking at.
Who's not in this post
Grudens. Before Jon Gruden was outed as an alarmingly racist dude, every single hot board nationwide had him on it for Reasons that remain obscure to me. Your Urban Meyers, Nick Sabans, and whoever else might be tanned, rested, and ready to leave broadcasting are not in this post because all of these folks are 1) deeply unlikely and 2) bad ideas. Also Michigan is not going to pick a dude off the retirement scrap heap one year after doing that to literally incredible results.
Harbaughs. Jay, Jim, John: not happening. Neither is the recently fired Minnesota OC.
DeBoers. IE: established, sitting head coaches at power programs. For purposes of this post Indiana counts as a power program, I guess?
Eli Drinkwitz. What an ass.
Setting the stage
The relative good news is that there is not a job out there particularly close to Michigan and it doesn't look like there will be one opening up. Four P4 jobs have come open; NC State has already gone for program legend and certain failure Phillip Rivers. Baylor and Maryland will not be relevant for Michigan's search. Florida State might be, but the program's constant caterwauling about the ACC and the fact that they held on to Mike Norvell for so long imply that the financial commitment isn't in the same realm as Michigan.
A brief survey of the omnipresent Hot Seat articles shows a few other SEC/B10 programs to think about: USC, Clemson, and Wisconsin. Wisconsin is only relevant because one of the candidates below is Jason Eck, who may prefer a homecoming to resources. USC probably isn't going to be in the market because Lincoln Riley's buyout is supposedly around 70 million. Clemson could be a complicating factor, but if 247's budget estimate of 20-30 million is correct there will not be a program with anywhere near the financial muscle in the market this cycle.
What about extensions? This post will not be trucking with rumors of them. I'm not sure it will be trucking with actual signed ones that have not been FOIAed to determine whether they actually increase the coach in question's buyout meaningfully.
Who is in this post
in no particular order
JASON ECK, NEW MEXICO

[Barron]
Was a semi-popular name last year after Eck played to win in Michigan Stadium and led the Lobos to a 9-4 year that is vastly above their historical baseline. 8-2 this year and had UNM ranked for the first time in program history before a disappointing loss to UNLV last week.
Eck was a Wisconsin offensive lineman in the mid-90s who was an OL coach for almost 20 years; he was also an OC for five years in there before taking Idaho to three straight FCS playoff appearances. After he left, Idaho descended to 4-8; they're 5-6 this year.
FIT? Ex-Big Ten OL turned OL coach who looks like Kirby Smart, the most Big-Ten-coded coach outside the Big Ten? I'd say this tighter is than… I'd say it's pretty tight.
CAVEATS? Five years as a head coach at an FCS school and a low-major FBS school is a thin resume for the Michigan job… or at least it might have been in a different era. These days those thin resumes are going to be more prominent because poaching playoff coaches is going to be difficult if they're not Lane Kiffin.
Also, Eck has not coached at a school with one dollar to its name since he was a GA. These days I'm actually less worried about that than I might have been ten years ago, because if Eck shows up and does pretty well he'll have the money to recruit just fine. Still, there could be hiccups as Eck settles into a chair that does not have nails poking out of it.
BLOG REACTION IF HIRED? I'd be into it. The idea of an ex-OL seems extremely appealing after the disaster of this year. The Lobos are winning this season with a legit defense (#23 in adjusted EPA/play allowed, #1 in success rate allowed, #1 in havoc rate) that was assembled on a shoestring budget.
[After THE JUMP: other guys with plugged in headsets]
WILL STEIN, KENTUCKY
Former walk-on QB at Louisville has had a meteoric rise. In 2019 he was the offensive coordinator at Lake Travis. That is a high school. He hooked on at UTSA for three years, the first two as a passing game coordinator before a co-OC role in year three. Oregon then scooped him up as their OC for three years (Adj EPA/play ranks: 2nd, 2nd, 11th) before Kentucky made him their head guy.
The Wildcats are 7-3 in year one; their aEPA/play has gone from 71st to 33rd.
FIT? Stein doesn't have regional connections and makes his hay as a passing game dude so this one is a little fuzzy. Has been in the Big Ten for a bit, I guess.
CAVEATS? Well, obviously less than a season as a head coach and just three as a P4 OC means this resume is a lot of fairy dust and hope. The 'Cats signature wins are over then-#9 Texas A&M and then-#10 LSU, both outfits that clearly did not deserve their elevated rankings when the games were played. Shine has come off a bit after consecutive losses to Tennessee and Florida; not too hard to see Stein bang on the Mark Stoops 7-5 since UK's final two games are against Mizzou and Louisville.
BLOG REACTION IF HIRED? I was going to write something about how a lot of my enthusiasm hinges on the outcome of the next two games, but if my enthusiasm hinges on two games I'm going to say this one is premature.
BOB CHESNEY, UCLA

YouTube screenshot
Another guy literally in his first year as a P4 head coach. Chesney maintained Cignetti's JMU program more or less as-is. Cig in D-1: 8-3, 11-1, ranked #24. Chesney: 9-4, 12-2, ranked #20. Chesney's final JMU team was a hair better than Cignetti's, per SP+.  Then he arrived at UCLA and we are all aware of what is going on there: undefeated despite losing their starting quarterback midway through the year, playoff lock, best UCLA season since Troy Aikman was there, probably.
But wait, there's more. Before that Chesney was head coach at Holy Cross, Assumption, and Salve Regina. His 44-21 record at Holy Cross is a minor miracle. He took them to four of their six all time FCS playoff appearances and has the only two playoff wins in school history. Assumption is D-II and does not have a Wikipedia page for their football program. (Wikipedia does assert that the Greyhounds play at the alarmingly-named Brian Kelly Stadium—even more alarmingly, it is named after that Brian Kelly.)
FIT? Chesney was a D-III player in Pennsylvania and spent a lot of time on the East Coast over the course of his career, so he's probably familiar with Michigan sort of situations. Seth jested that his hair was too spiky but that was a jest.
CAVEATS? First year P4 head coach, I guess, but Cignetti just happened and he has had a ton of experience as a head coach at all levels except the P4.
BLOG REACTION IF HIRED? Toot toot. Chesney seems like the best combination of experience and results available.
JAKE DICKERT, WAKE FOREST
Dickert the Coachert was a WR at Wisconsin-Stevens Point, whereupon he embarked on a tour of Big Sky Country with a series of jobs in the Dakotas and other rural Western areas before hooking up with then-P5 Washington State. He was whistling innocently in Pullman when Nick Rolovich committed one of the stupidest bag fumbles of all time by refusing to get a COVID vaccine. WSU scuffled to a 3-3 finish under Dickert, then proceeded to go 7-6, 5-7, and 8-4 in extraordinarily fraught circumstances.
If that didn't look like a slam dunk P4 resume, Wake Forest did not care. They have been richly rewarded thus far, with a 9-4 2025 followed by Wake cracking the top ten at 9-1. Wake hasn't really beaten anyone to get to this point unless Louisville and SMU count, but of late they have been dump-trucking mid ACC teams like a contender should. 49-7 over SMU, 51-7 over Virginia, 41-7 over Cal, 38-14 over NC State, and 57-3 over Stanford is an eye-opening five-game run. (They also nuked Merrimack 77-0 in there.) A double OT escape from Purdue does give pause.
Still, Wake Forest is #7 in the latest SP+ rankings and this is the program's high water mark by an incredible margin since 1970:

FIT? Seems fine enough to me.
CAVEATS? Dickert's tenure at WSU wasn't great, though he has to be graded on a curve since he was piloting a team saddled by the fact that they were leaving the power conferences. A two year ACC tenure is also a little less than definitive.
BLOG REACTION IF HIRED? Immediately improving Wake to about as good as they've ever been and then vastly exceeding it seems pretty good to me. The resume is thin but pretty much everyone on this list has a thin resume.
JEFF BROHM, LOUISVILLE

[Bryan Fuller]
He's back! Brohm has pretty much all of the assets and drawbacks he had a year ago. Louisville is currently 7-3, having lost those three games by exactly a field goal each. They're 17th in SP+ with the #5 offense in the country and the #41 defense. Unlike ~everyone else on this list Brohm has been a Big Ten head coach, battling to a 36-34 record with Purdue. If that doesn't impress much, consider Purdue before and after Brohm.
At UL he's gone 10-4, 9-4, and 9-4 prior to this season—a solid tenure but not a HIRE ME NOW one. Still, after three years of largely unwatchable offense the idea of putting a guy who has undeniable offensive bonafides in charge appeals. The fantasy of pairing Brohm with Michigan's existing defensive staff is probably just that—a fantasy—but I'm going close my eyes and envision it for a moment. Yep. Feels nice.
FIT? Guy spent six years in West Lafayette so he'll know the region just fine. Identity as a pass-first Air Raid guy is in conflict with Michigan's traditional ground-and-pound, so that could be a problem.
CAVEATS? While Brohm has consistently overperformed with bottom-feeders his tenure at Louisville seems to be good but not great. UL has a lot of resources compared to much of their ACC competition. 247's attempt to place teams in funding tiers saw UL slot in a broad $20 million+ tier with half the league, behind only Miami. Brohm has not emerged from that chasing pack despite FSU and Clemson being down.
BLOG REACTION IF HIRED? Brohm became a persona non grata amongst some people during the last search for reasons that are obscure. I don't think he has the ceiling of a couple of guys on this list but he provides the highest floor. I'd probably be okay with it.
BRYANT HAINES, INDIANA DC
If there's a coordinator on the docket Haines is the hot name. Former Ball State linebacker has been Cignetti's DC since 2019 at JMU and Indiana. Upon his arrival he deployed the best IU defense in the history of SP+, which goes back to 1970 now. Not content with that, he won the Broyles award last year and actually seemed to deserve it; IU was second nationally in defensive SP+. They are second again this year.
Indiana's talent has had an uptick since NIL got going but the only defensive draftees off last year's team were CB D'Angelo Ponds, a second rounder, and LB Aiden Fisher, a seventh rounder. NFL Draft Buzz's 2027 projections have Jamari Sharpe as a late day two pick and then six or seven day three picks; that talent level is not "back to back #2 defenses" and it's likely that Haines has some Venables-like juice to him. Bill Radjewski has an extensive Bluesky thread on him that lays out the case.
FIT? He's currently at Indiana and went to Ball State so I think we're good here.
CAVEATS? Well, one: not a head coach yet. Radjewski also notes that previous DC to HC hires have largely been failures:
The precedent: Kirby Smart. Never a head coach; 8 seasons as Alabama's DC, all top 10 in EPA allowed. Georgia fell in Year 1, then +18 by Years 3–4. He's the exception. DCs hired into a top-third program's job, 2000–21: 2 of 18 left it better. 12 busted.

[image or embed]
— Bill Radjewski (@collegefootballdata.com) November 13, 2026 at 10:23 AM

He's either Kirby Smart or he's a disappointment.
BLOG REACTION IF HIRED? Hoo boy this would be a swing for the fences but his work with IU's defense makes it pretty enticing. This is his third year; he has the three best IU defenses since 1970 and this year and last they have been capital-E Elite without a single first round pick—and probably just two day two picks—on the roster.
ONE MAN'S TENTATIVE ORDER
Pending observation of Insta follows:
Bob Chesney
Jason Eck
Bryant Haines
Jake Dickert
Jeff Brohm
Will Stein

When things get this bad, things are fundamentally broken in psychological ways that are far beyond the scope of Upon Further Review. I look at film, count up good and bad things I see, and try to put those events in the context of what we know about these players to supply some kind of opinion about who they are on a football field. Count the half-assery and lost puppies on that play, and try to tie it to any event we've seen from these guys before it; you cannot.
One of the functions of sports fandom is to look for superhuman abilities that we admire in our athletes. The push-pull of that, especially for college football, is they're not superhumans, just people trying very hard to be. That instinct in you to go "oh FUCK THIS" hits them just as strongly, and then it's just their mental and cultural training that allows them to recenter and perform again. The physical and mental strain of trying to hold up Kyle Whittingham's program, a continent away from home, against players as talented as Oregon's is bound to crack. Even break a few times.
And for each guy it's different. Trey Pierce was his solid self, but for fewer snaps. Enow Etta was something less. Jonah Lea'ea stepped up.
